Level 1 (field) service covers reading LED and error code, pressing the button, repositioning bracket or magnet, releasing the tag in Tidewalk, and a restart by holding the button 10 seconds, without opening anything.
Level 2 (depot swap) covers replacing bracket KB4-D, magnet KM-2 and the housing screws kit, and changing the reporting interval with KC-Config, with the housing staying closed.
Hamburg-Waltershof, Rotterdam-Maasvlakte and Gothenburg-Arendal work at Level 2 only, except that Rotterdam may exchange batteries since March 2024.
Level 3 service, where the housing is opened, is done only by the Gdynia workshop called Bay 3 in building GDY-1.
Bay 3 has two certified technicians and a third in training, and in September 2024 the person responsible for Bay 3 is Wiktor Szymaniak-Reyes.
The KC-Tag 4 contains one primary, non-rechargeable lithium thionyl chloride cell (Voltrac VB-36L), which must never be charged, shorted, heated above +85 °C, crushed or punctured.
A hot, swollen or leaking cell goes immediately into the sand bucket next to the door of Bay 3 and the workshop lead is informed.

A burning lithium cell is fought with the class D extinguisher at the bay entrance (red with a yellow label), not water or the CO2 extinguisher, and the labels were made yellow after a 2023 drill mistake.
Work with opened housings requires an ESD-safe workstation with a wrist strap with a 1 MΩ series resistor.
The workshop climate is 18 to 26 °C and 30 to 60 % relative humidity, and below 30 % RH the ionizer fan must be on.
Opened boards are placed only on the grey conductive mat, and cleaning uses isopropyl alcohol of at least 99 %, never acetone because it clouds the sensor cap.
Torque screwdriver TS-04 covers 0.2 to 1.2 N·m and is calibrated every 6 months.
Torque screwdriver TS-07 covers 0.05 to 0.30 N·m and is for the small board screws only.
The Torx T6 bit for the housing screws is replaced after 400 openings; T15 is for bracket screws and T3 for the sensor board retainer screws.
The dry-block calibrator is the TB-120 with stability of ±0.02 °C at the three calibration points.
The reference probe is RX-400, serial 88213, with calibration due 2025-02.
The humidity chamber is HC-2, 4-litre, with two salt jars of LiCl and NaCl solutions.
The housing leak test uses the pressure decay tester PD-25.
The programming cable is KC-PROG-1 (USB to UART with pogo adapter) and the workshop laptop image is WS-2023-11 with KC-Service Tool v1.14.
The battery passivation test uses a 1 kΩ, 0.25 W load resistor with clips.
Consumables per opening are one gasket G-4 (silicone cord seal, cord diameter 2.0 mm), six housing screws and an opening seal sticker.
Housing screws are M2 × 8 with Torx T6 head, reused at most three times, after which the screws kit KSK-4 (six M2 × 8 plus four M1.6 × 4) is fitted.
The gasket G-4 is single use, always, even if it looks perfect after opening.
The KC-Tag 4 serial number form is KT4-YYWW-NNNNN: two-digit year, calendar week of final test, and a running number that restarts every year.
Serial KT4-2335-00712 was tested in week 35 of 2023 and was the 712th unit that year.
The KC-Tag 4 label is laser engraved on the rear next to the bracket guide, repeated in a QR code, and shows hardware revision and radio variant 868.
The 2024 running numbers reach about 03000 by September, which is why the Tidewalk database field was widened from 4 to 5 digits.
The KC-Tag 4 main board is MB-4R2-C and holds the MCU, radio, BLE, flash memory and the Hall door sensor.
The KC-Tag 4 sensor board is SNS-4R2-B, with temperature and humidity sensor on a flexible arm to the sensor cap.
The KC-Tag 4 antenna is the flex antenna ANT1 fixed to the inside of the lid, for 868 MHz.
The KC-Tag 4 housing set is KH4-R2 (lid, base, sensor cap, latch) and the battery is VB-36L, 3.6 V, 2,600 mAh.
On R1 units the sensor board is SNS-4R1-A and cannot be exchanged with the R2 part.

R2 introduced gold-plated battery contact springs, while R1 has nickel springs that corrode in salty atmospheres, the main reason for the 'random reset' tickets from Baltic customers in 2022 and 2023.
Before opening, the technician records the serial, reads error code and firmware with command ver, and dumps memory with mem dump if the customer wants the data.
The clock of the KC-Tag 4 is lost if the battery is removed for more than 20 minutes.
The tag is taken off the bracket by pushing the latch down with a small screwdriver and sliding the tag upwards by about 8 mm.
The six housing screws are numbered 1 to 6 on the rear and are loosened in the sequence 6-5-4-3-2-1.
The sensor arm is attached to the lid, not the base, and its flex arm is only 34 mm long and tears if the base is rotated against the lid.
After removing the gasket G-4 the groove is checked for dirt and salt crystals and cleaned with swab and isopropyl alcohol.
The battery connector BT1 is a two-pin polarised connector, pulled by the plug and not the wires.
The flex connector J3 latch opens by about 90 degrees; breaking it makes the main board MB-4R2-C scrap, the most expensive mistake in Bay 3.
The antenna cable at the u.FL connector ANT1 is released with a plastic spudger, never with tweezers.
The sensor board is held in the lid by four retainer screws M1.6 × 4 removed with the T3 bit.
A normal opening including reading the data takes about 9 minutes, and if it takes longer than 15 minutes the technician should ask for help.
A trainee in July spent 40 minutes on a J3 connector that was already open, which led to the 15-minute rule being written into the manual.
Gunnar notes that terminals of a removed cell must be taped before it goes into bin L-3, because a yellow-lid bin once got warm on a Monday morning.
During reassembly the sensor flex enters J3 with contacts facing down and the antenna cable is clipped in before the battery is connected.
The housing screws are tightened in sequence 1-4-2-5-3-6 in two passes, 0.15 N·m then 0.35 N·m, and the second pass must follow within 5 minutes.
Housing screws (6 pcs, M2 × 8, Torx T6) are tightened to 0.35 N·m with TS-07.
Sensor board retainer screws (4 pcs, M1.6 × 4, Torx T3) are tightened to 0.12 N·m.
Bracket screws KB4-D (4 pcs, M4 × 12, Torx T15) are tightened to 1.2 N·m with a maximum of 1.5 N·m using TS-04.
The pole clamp screw of the optional pole adapter is M5 × 20 at 2.0 N·m.
The pole adapter is a customer-specific item used by the Kłaipėda yard for its stack-end poles and is not part of the standard product.
The leak test uses 25 kPa overpressure, a 20-second stabilisation time and a 45-second measuring time.
A tag passes the leak test if the pressure drop in the measuring time is not larger than 0.8 kPa.
A tag failing the leak test is reopened once with the gasket exchanged; if it fails a second time the housing set KH4-R2 is replaced.
A tag that passed the leak test gets a round white opening seal sticker with the Korvane logo and the date in DD.MM.YY format over screw number 3; a tag without it is considered not serviced.
Since March 2024 the Rotterdam depot technicians Sanne Verhoeven and Bas Okonkwo-Pruis may replace batteries because of the roughly 600 tags a year that would otherwise go to Gdynia.
Rotterdam has its own PD-25 leak tester with serial 0412 and sends the job cards monthly to Bay 3 for filing.
A good new Voltrac VB-36L reads at least 3.55 V open-circuit; a lower cell is returned to the supplier.
Cells older than 18 months from the manufacture date are not fitted even if the voltage is fine.
After a battery replacement the command batt reset resets the battery gauge and writes the replacement date into the tag.
The battery change is entered in Tidewalk under menu Device, Service, Battery changed, done by the workshop at the end of the day.
Replaced cells get tape on both terminals and go into bin L-3 (yellow lid), collected by the waste contractor on the first Tuesday of each month.
For a new cell older than 12 months from manufacture, a 1 kΩ load is applied for 30 seconds and the voltage is measured again 10 seconds after unloading.
A passivation-tested cell is rejected if its voltage is not back above 3.50 V.
Firmware 2.6 and later shows error E04 if the voltage under radio load is below 3.0 V, and E04 on a brand-new battery is nearly always a passivated cell.
Tidewalk creates a battery ticket when the battery estimate is below 15 % and the workshop plans replacement within 60 days.
A tag with E04 must be replaced within 5 working days.
For customers with a pharma clause such as Helvetia Pharma Logistik GmbH, batteries are replaced at 20 % remaining, configured in the Tidewalk customer profile and not in the tag.
KC-Tag 4 firmware has a bootloader (version 1.3 in all R2 units) and an application image delivered as kt4_fw_<version>_r2.bin, for example kt4_fw_2.9.0_r2.bin, with a .sig file.
The bootloader checks the image signature against the public key with ID KCSIG-2023-B and refuses images signed with another key, possibly showing E11.
SHA-256 hashes of released images are kept in the release record by the Hardware Engineering team, and the support team does not hold them.
The latest released firmware on 18 September 2024 is 2.9.0, and the oldest version still usable with the KC-Hub 200 is 2.4.

fact: UART flashing is used when the tag shows E11, when over-the-air update fails, or when a tag is new from the board stage with no application.
The KC-PROG-1 pogo adapter goes on the six gold programming pads J5 next to the antenna connector, pad 1 marked with a triangle.
The J5 pad assignment is 1 = 3V3, 2 = TX, 3 = RX, 4 = GND, 5 = BOOT, 6 = RESET.
To enter the bootloader, hold the button, short pad BOOT to GND and release the button, after which the LED alternates red and green.
UART flashing runs at 115,200 baud and a full image of about 212 KB takes approximately 38 seconds.
Calibration data survives an application update because it is kept in a separate flash page, but mem erase deletes logged data and needs customer permission.
If the UART write is interrupted the tag shows alternating red-green indefinitely, which is not a defect; the technician restarts at step 4.
Over-the-air updates are started from Tidewalk (Fleet, Firmware campaigns) and at most 20 tags per hub are updated at the same time because of the 868 MHz radio duty cycle.
A tag takes part in an OTA campaign only if its battery estimate is at least 30 % and last-reported battery voltage at least 3.3 V.
An over-the-air update of one KC-Tag 4 takes about 11 minutes during which the LED alternates red and green.
When an OTA campaign fails for a tag three times in a row the tag goes on the list 'OTA failed' and a support case with priority P3 is opened automatically.
OTA failures are mostly caused by a weak radio link of 80 metres or more in a stack with the hub behind a reefer wall.
After a firmware change the clock must be within 5 seconds of hub time and the door sensor must react when the magnet is moved away by 15 mm.
values: within 5 seconds of the hub time

fact: A KC-Tag 4 is calibrated at the factory and then once every 12 months, as a three-point temperature check and two-point humidity check.
The calibration certificate template is KC-CAL-T and 2024 certificate numbers have the form KCC-2024-NNNNN.
A tag whose last calibration is older than 13 months shows error E12.
For pharma-contract customers Tidewalk raises a warning 45 days before the calibration certificate expires.
Calibration is done only in Bay 3; Rotterdam has no calibration equipment.
Before calibration, tags are conditioned at 20 to 24 °C for at least 2 hours after cold storage because condensation inside the sensor cap makes them read wrong.
Up to 12 tags are placed in the TB-120 insert together with the RX-400 reference probe in the central hole.
Calibration points are run in the order +40.0 °C, 0.0 °C, −25.0 °C, hot first because the block cools slower than it heats, saving about 40 minutes per batch.
At each point the block must be stable within ±0.02 °C for 5 minutes, followed by a soak time of 25 minutes before reading the tags.
The calibration offset is the tag reading minus the reference reading.
values: tag reading minus the reference reading

fact: An absolute offset up to 0.25 °C at every point is 'As found: OK', with offsets stored and a certificate issued.
An offset above 0.25 °C and up to 0.80 °C is 'Adjusted', written with cal set, re-measured, with a residual offset of 0.10 °C or less.
An absolute offset above 0.80 °C is 'Rejected': sensor board SNS-4R2-B is replaced and full calibration repeated.
A serial rejected twice is scrapped with scrap form WF-22 and goes to the recycling box.
For R1 units the limit between OK and Adjusted is 0.40 °C instead of 0.25 °C because of the older sensor.
The expanded uncertainty on the certificate for temperature points is ±0.08 °C (k = 2).
The reference probe RX-400 is calibrated by an external accredited laboratory every 12 months, with the next date February 2025.
Humidity is checked at +25 °C in chamber HC-2 with lithium chloride giving 11.3 % RH and sodium chloride giving 75.3 % RH.
Tags stay in each salt jar for 4 hours because 3 hours is not enough for the sensor to settle.
The humidity acceptance limit is ±2.0 % RH at both points, and an out-of-limit tag is adjusted with cal set hum.

Humidity adjustment is done only for customers needing humidity such as Brunnen & Sohn Frischdienst and pharma customers; others are adjusted only if the offset is bigger than 5 % RH, with a note on the certificate.
The calibration certificate lists serial, date, technician, reference probe and serial, three temperature offsets as found and adjusted, humidity offsets, result and next due date.
values: three temperature offsets as found and after adjustment

fact: Calibration records are kept for 7 years and the paper originals are in the grey cabinet of Bay 3, shelf 2.
Calibration work stops when the reference probe, dry-block or either torque screwdriver is overdue for calibration.
In Tree A, a battery below 2.5 V is replaced, 2.5 V to 3.55 V gets the passivation test, and above 3.55 V leads to the contact check.
Rotterdam found the red pull-tab still in place on tags three times in one week of 2023.
values: three times in one week of 2023

fact: On R1 units the battery spring set is replaced if it shows green corrosion, and if the tag is still dark the main board MB-4R2-C is replaced.
One short green flash every 5 seconds means hub in contact so the problem is not the radio, while two flashes mean no hub contact.
values: one short flash every 5 seconds (hub in contact)

fact: A tag stays paired to the old hub until released in Tidewalk, and the radio test places the tag within 5 metres of the hub with a 10-second button restart.
A loose u.FL antenna connector reduces the range to under 10 metres and is the number one reason for 'works on the bench, not in the yard'.
The rf test command must show a transmit power of +14 dBm ±1.5 dB, otherwise the main board is replaced.
A difference below 0.6 °C is within the datasheet outside the main band and below 0.3 °C inside it, so it is not a fault; comparison runs at least 30 minutes.
A sensor cap with condensation is dried 24 hours at 40 °C; if condensation returns the gasket is leaking.
The sensor line voltage read with sns raw at 25 °C must be 1.318 V ±0.020 V, otherwise sensor board SNS-4R2-B is replaced.
Firmware 2.7 or later filters single-sample temperature spikes caused by radio bursts, tracked as bug ID KCF-1421.
On a steel door with a heavy gasket frame that holds it 10 mm open when closed, a shim set of 3 shims of 2 mm is used under the magnet.
Other magnets such as the magnetic latch of a neighbouring container must be kept 100 mm from the Hall sensor.
The door raw command should read between 340 and 420 counts with the door closed and above 900 when open, otherwise the Hall sensor is faulty and the main board is replaced.
Since firmware 2.9 a door that stays open longer than 20 minutes raises a 'door left open' alarm, which is a feature and not a fault.
The battery life table in the quick start guide assumes a hub at 60 metres and +5 °C, and a 2-minute interval gives at best 11 months.
At −25 °C or colder take 35 % off the battery life table, and a tag unable to reach the hub does up to 3 transmissions per report.
Sleep current measured with pwr sleep must be below 8 µA; 8 to 25 µA suggests moisture, and above 25 µA the main board is replaced.
A tag with a drain larger than 12 % per month is replaced and the old cell goes to the quality lab, where Benedikta Aaltonen asks for at least 5 samples a quarter.
For errors E01 and E02 the workshop opens the tag, checks the J3 latch and flex, reseats it, and replaces SNS-4R2-B if the code remains.
For error E03 the workshop dries the sensor board 24 hours at 40 °C and replaces SNS-4R2-B if the code remains.
values: Dry the sensor board 24 hours at 40 °C

fact: For error E05 the workshop does a UART reflash and mem erase with customer permission, and replaces MB-4R2-C if the code returns.
For error E07 the workshop sets the clock with rtc set and replaces MB-4R2-C if drift returns within 7 days.
Error E08 is a hub fault, not a tag fault; E09 is hub capacity; E10 is mounting; E11 needs a UART reflash; E12 needs calibration.
values: Hub fault, not a tag fault

In the door test the magnet is moved from 5 mm to 15 mm at minute 100 and the door-open event must show in Tidewalk within 5 seconds.
After warm-up of 30 minutes humidity is compared with the room hygrometer within ±5 % RH, and passing tags get the label 'FT OK'.

fact: The KC-Hub 200 measures 220 × 140 × 48 mm without antenna and weighs 1.1 kg.

The KC-Hub 200 supports Power over Ethernet IEEE 802.3af class 3 with typical consumption 6.4 W and maximum 9.8 W.

The KC-Hub 200 uplink buffer holds up to 72 hours of reports from 250 tags and the firmware in January 2024 was 3.4.2.
The hub must not be installed inside a container stack because steel walls shield the radio waves.
The hub must be mounted at least 3.0 m above ground and not higher than 8 m, because above 8 m PoE voltage drop becomes a problem.
The antenna must point vertically upwards with at least 0.5 m free space to any metal surface.
The hub must not be installed directly above a reefer unit because of electromagnetic noise from the compressor drives and inverters.
Depot rule of thumb is one hub per yard area of about 180 m radius in the open, and one per every second block of stacks if stacks are higher than three containers.
A Korvane service radio survey with a test tag costs EUR 210.00 per half day plus travel.
Pole band screws of the hub mounting plate are tightened to 4.0 N·m, without an impact driver, because too-tight bands deform thin lighting poles.
The hub's lock screw at the bottom of the mounting plate is tightened to 1.8 N·m.
The SMA antenna is screwed on by hand plus a quarter turn with a spanner, never with a tool on the antenna body.
For wall mounting the drill holes are 120 mm apart horizontally and 90 mm vertically, and on a metal wall a spacer of at least 30 mm is used.
The 1U shelf KH2-R1U holds up to two hubs side by side and is fixed to a 19-inch rack with four M6 screws at 5.0 N·m.
Indoors the antenna must be taken out on the extension cable ANT-EXT-3 (3 m, loss 0.9 dB) to a window or roof.

PoE cable must be Cat5e or better with a maximum length of 100 m between injector or switch and hub.
Cables leaving a building need a surge protector SP-PoE-1 at the building entry and a second one at the hub if the pole is higher than 6 m.
In summer 2023 surge protection saved three hubs in the Rotterdam yard during a thunderstorm and became standard.
When both DC and PoE are connected the hub takes the DC input and PoE is standby, a design wish of the Gothenburg depot.
LAN1 is an RJ45 1 Gbit/s port used as PoE input and uplink.

The USB-C port is for service only, as technician console and firmware recovery.
The RS-485 two-pin terminal block is reserved for door controller integration and disabled in firmware 3.4.2.
The SMA port is a 50 ohm antenna connector and the nano-SIM slot behind a cover exists only on units with option H2-LTE.
The hub gets its address by DHCP, and a fixed address can be set in its web interface on port 8080.
The factory hostname of the hub is kch200- followed by the last 6 characters of its MAC address.
The hub needs outbound TCP 8883 (MQTT over TLS), TCP 443 for firmware downloads and UDP 123 for NTP, with no inbound ports.

The monitoring FAQ was last reviewed on 5 September 2024 by Customer Support Engineering and applies to KC-Tag 4 hardware R2 with firmware 2.8 or newer and KC-Hub 200 with firmware 3.4 or newer.
A new KC-Tag 4 that seems dead usually still has the red pull-tab in the battery compartment; after pulling it the LED goes amber for two seconds and then green.
If the LED stays dark the user should press the button for one second, and only if there is still no light write to support with the serial number from the calibration card.
With the factory interval of 10 minutes the KC-Tag 4 battery lasts about 38 months, at 30 minutes 61 months and at 2 minutes only 11 months.
In a freezer at −25 °C or colder the battery life is reduced by roughly a third, and opening the tag voids the warranty.
The tag is fitted 1.4 metres above the floor on the door frame with the magnet on the leaf that opens first, and the pole adapter is a special item supplied on request, used by the Kłaipėda yard.
Two green blinks mean the tag cannot reach the hub but is storing readings, normal for a container on a ship or inside a stack.
values: on a ship or inside a stack

fact: Amber blinking once every ten seconds means battery under 20 %, and blinking twice means a limit has been exceeded.
Since firmware 2.8 the KC-Tag 4 pairing window is 180 seconds, while the older guide Rev. D still says 120 seconds, correct for older firmware.
Pairing means holding the tag button 4 seconds, pressing PAIR on the hub for 2 seconds, and staying within about 5 metres.
One KC-Hub 200 handles 250 tags, the 251st tag gets error E09, and old tags are released in Tidewalk via Devices → Release.
The hub normally uses PoE 802.3af class 3 with typical consumption 6.4 W, alternatively the box PoE injector or a 12–24 V DC supply, with an Ethernet cable shorter than 100 metres.
The hub needs outbound TCP 8883 to hubs-in.tidewalk.korvane.example, TCP 443 for firmware and UDP 123 for time, and a TLS-resigning transparent proxy is not trusted by the hub.
An amber CLOUD lamp on the hub means no Tidewalk connection, usually port 8883 blocked, and the hub buffers up to 72 hours of reports from 250 tags.
The tag measures every 30 seconds and on a limit excess reports every 60 seconds, so an alarm appears in Tidewalk typically within about a minute and a half if the hub is in contact.
values: about a minute and a half

fact: Since firmware 2.9 an alarm is repeated every 60 seconds until somebody acknowledges it.
A 'door left open' alarm means the door was open for more than 20 minutes, introduced with firmware 2.9 in August 2024, and the limit is not customer-changeable yet.
The tag stores 65,536 readings, about 22.7 days at 30 seconds, and shows E06 when memory is more than 98 % full.
Accuracy is ±0.3 °C between −25 and +40 °C, ±0.6 °C outside that band, and ±3 % RH for humidity between 20 and 80 % RH.
Error E12 means the calibration is older than 13 months, since the 12-month certificate gets one month of tolerance.
Recalibration takes 15 working days, or 3 working days with the express service for EUR 45.00 per tag, and Tidewalk subscribers get the first renewal free.
The warranty is 24 months from delivery for tag and hub, the battery is not covered, and bracket screws tightened above 1.5 N·m are a customer cause.
Defective tags are accepted only with an RMA number at the Gdynia goods receipt, Monday to Friday 07:30 to 15:30, and unannounced shipments go back at the sender's expense.
KC-Tag 3 repairs end on 31 December 2024 and Tidewalk support continues until 31 December 2025.
Returning KC-Tag 3 loggers earns a trade-in credit of EUR 38.00 per piece on an order of at least 10 KC-Tag 4, and the hub needs the 433 MHz option H2-433 to hear a KC-Tag 3.
KC-Tag 3 and KC-Tag 4 can share a hub only if it has the 433 MHz module; the KC-Tag 3 reports every 15 minutes.

Typical first reply time from support is 4 working hours, and for P1 tickets (cargo at risk) the target is 30 minutes.
